In algorithmic literature, the linear time class is commonly abbreviated as LIN. Over the past ten years, researchers have used LIN to classify problems by linearity. Despite its ubiquity, LIN's precise composition remains unclear. This study offers an exact characterization of LIN using randomness and ordered assignments, and also introduces a corresponding characterization for BPL without relying on previously complex assumptions.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative method in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We develop an algorithm to compute period integrals graph-theoretically,
applicable to Feynman integrals and related calculations. This method relies
on expansions of differential forms over graph subdivisions, yielding compact
expressions as linear combinations of Lindelöf extensions of multiple zeta values.
To illustrate, we apply the algorithm explicitly to all two-loop graphs,
examine its general features and discuss possible approaches to more complex cases.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement.  This evidence confirms our hypothesis that auxiliary variables play a vital role in decoding and object categorization.

We investigate the topological characteristics of one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems with correlations. Unlike the case of non-spectrally equivalent unitary operators, the winding numbers of two distinct non-Hermitian systems with different spectra cannot always be considered equivalent. Introducing correlations reduces the topological classification from a single winding number to a pair of winding numbers. We demonstrate that even when the winding numbers are identical, the winding numbers of individual subsystems can vary with the introduction of correlations. Furthermore, we show that for certain classes of non-Hermitian systems with time-reversal and particle-hole symmetries, the winding numbers are not the sole determining factor for topological classification when correlations are involved. Consequently, systems with the same winding numbers may not be topologically classified as they can exhibit different behaviors upon the introduction of random phases.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained prominence due to their applications in omnidirectional precoding. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and explores their connections with various mathematical structures including sequences, matrices, and higher-dimensional arrays. Building on this, specific constructions of these matrices are presented for specific dimensions. Furthermore, a novel class of Golay complementary matrices is introduced, called balanced Golay complementary arrays, with provided construction methods for specific dimensions. Balanced arrays with minimal imbalance are also defined and their relationships to higher-dimensional Golay complementary arrays are demonstrated through the use of constructed examples.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS and LHCb data from 13 TeV, specifically focusing on the LHCb and CMS Collaborators' 2016 through 2018 activities. By analyzing the number of Higgs bosons created in an alternative to the standard model, a constrained width of 0.0949 MeV was found. By applying various mass assumptions, this width can be modified. When the Higgs boson interacts with other particles in a manner similar to the standard model, its width is approximately 4.1 times the standard model prediction. This result is achieved without making assumptions about the Higgs boson's self-coupling, instead, multiple self-coupling assumptions are explored in an extension of the standard model. Based on this analysis, an upper limit of 7.1 times the standard model prediction was set for the self-coupling. By combining the modified width with constraints on the modified coupling, a limit of 5.6 times the standard model prediction was established for the self-coupling.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperformed current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across diverse datasets.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$ of squares and let $r_{\mathcal{S}}(n)$ denote the number of times a natural number $n$ can be represented as a sum of squares from the set $\mathcal{S}$. It has been proven by Hardy and Littlewood that the maximum value of the function $r_{\mathcal{S}}$ is approximately proportional to constant times the square root of $n$. In contrast, our study demonstrates that for an additive complement $\mathcal{A}$ of the set $\mathcal{E}$, consisting of integers of the form $2^k m$, where $m$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and such that the greatest divisor of $m$ that is a power of $2$ is equal to $1$, the function $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n)$ is superlinearly growing for a sufficiently large $n$. Our study also examines the average values of $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n)$ and finds that it is also superlinearly growing for a sufficiently large $N$. Moreover, our study is supported by numerical computations that indicate the additive sets with the minimal possible values of the function $r_{\mathcal{A}}(n)$ exhibit a periodic structure with a period of $8$.

Quantum tunneling and resonance tunneling are fundamental phenomena that underpin many quantum phenomena. In solid-state systems, tunning can be triggered by perturbations to a quantum state, not just variations in barriers or particle energies. Focusing on silicon, which contains abundant isotopes with distinct nuclear spin properties that interact with electrons and atomic nuclei through magnetic couplings, we investigate how a phosphorus dopant in silicon can experience tuning without an external influence. We find that this perturbation can be caused by changes in the relative positions of atomic nuclei in silicon, specifically that of a neon atom, and that this tuning is an intrinsic property resulting from nuclear spin fluctuations.

A benchmark framework called LibOPT was designed to test the performance of a broad range of optimization algorithms across multiple disciplines, including combinatorial, convex, and non-convex nonlinear optimization problems. This framework facilitates testing of these algorithms on a single hardware platform or across a distributed cluster of multiple computers. LibOPT's comprehensive suite contains more than 100 algorithms for solving over 40 benchmark problems, and this paper serves as a starting point for evaluating the efficiency and robustness of this suite. Performance results using specific problems will be showcased to demonstrate the potential of automated testing pipelines for optimization software. These results also establish a baseline for future research, allowing for continuous improvement of the library's performance over time.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree of X. This concept helps us understand a key characteristic of a specific type of Fano varieties, known as Mukai varieties, which consist of several distinct types. We identify that nearly all of these varieties have a transitivity degree of one, with the exception of types F44 and F62-2, allowing us to fully complete the list of Fano -rvos of basic type that have a positive transitivity degree.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by a non-abelian space symmetry group where the product of functions follows the rules of non-abelian convolution. The group's action on multi-particle states leads to a situation where the state becomes independent of how it's formed, effectively destroying the concept of identical particles. The的程度 of this effect is controlled by a small parameter in the convolution. The phenomenon is also observed when considering higher-order effects of angular momentum.

We present a novel technique combining optical manipulation and detection to study
the transport properties of a semiconductor on a mesoscopic scale.
This method relies on two-photon absorption to excite and investigate charge
transport in wide bandgap materials.
A wide bandgap semiconductor, gallium nitride, is used to test the technique's
efficiency.
By projecting a patterned laser beam onto the material, we generate localized charge
carriers which are subsequently produced via a Hall effect, detected with single photon
detectors, and counted at room temperature.
Our findings demonstrate the capability to map the electric current with micrometer-scale
spatial resolution.
Additionally, the method allows for the extraction of a fundamental transport parameter,
the mobility, with high spatial resolution.
This technique is versatile and can be used to characterize a wide range of semiconductor
materials while offering detailed insight into electrical transport properties with precise
spatial resolution.
On a technological level, this method has the potential to serve as a diagnostic tool in
microfabrication processes.

Social media platforms are teeming with detrimental content, such as hateful content, which encompasses hate speech, racist language, sexist language, and hate-motivated speech. This kind of content frequently testifies to real-world hate crimes and is often a target of legal action. Identifying such content online not only aids in uncovering hidden patterns of hate but also helps to map its evolution over time. Prior research has utilized statistical analysis to determine the prevalence of hate speech on social media; however, this approach often relies on a limited understanding of the context and may overlook nuances in language. This study aims to provide a more in-depth examination of hate speech on social media by integrating automated detection with human-led qualitative analysis, focusing on Twitter data from the elections in France and the Netherlands. By doing so, we can gain a more comprehensive insight into the characteristics of hate speech in the digital age.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect on policy updates and results in more resilient controllers. In addition, our findings highlight the practical advantages of this approach in a simulation-based evaluation.

In centralized coded caching, incurring transmission costs is acceptable in exchange for reducing latency during networked wireless network file requests. A common strategy involves storing previously requested files in anticipation of future demands, utilizing previously sent files to satisfy current file requests through network coding. This research explores the optimization of storage-retrieval trade-offs in wireless networks by examining the centralized coded caching problem, where all users collaborate to maximize storage efficiency and minimize retrieval times. Specific objectives include caching popular files to serve multiple users simultaneously and coordinating users' transmissions to simultaneously send files to multiple users at once. We introduce a novel approach that combines collaboration and coordination to trade storage for retrieval times, allowing users to retrieve files in multiple generations instead of just one, and then retrieve as many generations as possible in a single transmission. This approach yields improved results, demonstrating reduced retrieval times compared to existing approaches in similar scenarios.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in PCF within Coq, providing a rigorous proof that the lifting monad is an optimal solution to the equation $T^{\omega}X = !^{\omega}X$. This hands-on definition serves as a non-compositional model that successfully integrates with the Coq-based "MC2" machine for model checking, as demonstrated in Gherghetti, Giarrò, and Munch's research in LICS 2019.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots is a challenging task, especially when the robot operates in an environment with uncertain sensor readings and moving obstacles. This difficulty is compounded by the fact that traditional model predictive control approaches, which rely on predicting the future locations of obstacles, are subject to significant forecasting errors. In this research, a new control method is proposed that utilizes an information exchange technique to accurately predict the future trajectories of obstacles. This approach involves sharing and updating the estimated states of obstacles with neighboring obstacles, as well as using a special filter to reduce noise in the predictions. Furthermore, the proposed method incorporates a safety mechanism into the control system's performance, providing formal guarantees of its correctness. The effectiveness of this control method has been confirmed through extensive computer simulations, in which the mobile robot successfully navigates around static and moving obstacles without any collisions.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on a set of equations that can't be experimentally tested, which raises the question of whether these processes should be viewed as interferometric events in nonlinear quantum mechanics. We investigate this question by analyzing the behavior of an optical quantum interferometer and a system governed by the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, which is also quantizable. The analysis reveals that, when it comes to linear quantum mechanics, nonlinear features can only be detected through specific phase preparation, measurement choices, and classical normalization techniques. These discoveries imply that current experiments in quantum interferometry and information processing can be reinterpreted as nonlinear quantum mechanics experiments, which is significant because it questions the perceived benefits of quantum information processing in these contexts.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications to complex numbers, with polynomial system solving being the underlying mechanism. The solution space of a polynomial system can generally be represented as a one-dimensional geometric structure, with the general methods utilizing a subset of properties that correspond to a non-degenerate subset of the system. Despite extensive research by computer algebra communities, efforts to eliminate the non-degenerate subset have generally focused solely on algebraic aspects of the solution space and have involved significant computational overhead. This paper proposes novel numerical methods tailored for real-world applications that target a specific non-degenerate subset of the system, with the primary goal being speed and robustness. By employing this approach, it becomes possible to resolve previously unsolvable polynomial systems. We showcase a benchmark study that demonstrates the method's effectiveness along with strategies to mitigate common numerical challenges. Furthermore, an open-source software tool enabling its numerical implementation is presented as a complement to an existing computer algebra tool already employed in numerous applications.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T$ below 10 GeV/c in $\sqrt{s_{_{\mathrm{NN}}}} = 200$ GeV Cu+Cu collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The number of produced photons significantly exceeds expectations from nucleon-nucleon collisions, particularly at low $p_T$. A strong correlation exists between low-$p_T$ photon yield and that of other particles, following a systematic law. This observation aligns with calculations from perturbative QCD, indicating a significant role for parton-parton interactions and a $d\hat{\sigma}/dy$ cross-section that is 1.5 times larger than in p+p collisions.

The Turan problem for three unoriented edges concerns finding the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free 3-uniform hypergraph. In 2022, Mubayi and Zhao discovered a solution to this problem, proving that the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free 3-uniform hypergraph with n vertices is at most n^2/2 + O(n^{8/5}). This paper presents a novel approach to part of their result, demonstrating that the sum of the third-degree values of all first-degree values of H is at most 2n^2 for such a hypergraph. The computation of this sum is based on the concept of complete bipartite graphs and its related parameters. Specifically, it is based on the idea of a dense graph and its related parameters, including its edge count, maximum degree, and codegree squared sum. By applying this sum, it is shown that a triangle-free 3-uniform hypergraph with n vertices has at most 2n^2 edges. This approach provides an alternative to the original proof by Mubayi and Zhao, and also reveals a relationship between the parameters of a hypergraph and its dual graph. Furthermore, it is shown that a triangle-free 3-uniform hypergraph with n vertices has at most 2n^2 edges, which leads to the conclusion that the Turan number for such a hypergraph is at most 2n^2. Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying complex images like maps on digital devices is challenging when the device's resolution doesn't align with the image resolution. This challenge arises from the need to balance anti-aliasing techniques that simulate smooth edge transitions without significantly impacting system efficiency. This paper proposes an innovative anti-aliasing technique specifically designed for vector maps, enhancing their visual appeal while maintaining system efficiency. Our approach leverages the concept of color blending across geometric shapes and edge properties. Extensive testing with real-world applications like navigation systems and digital signage demonstrates the technique's effectiveness in improving visual resolution and anti-aliasing while maintaining a low performance cost of around 6%. Furthermore, the proposed method can be extended to other applications, exploring new potential uses for vector-based vectoring.

This research presents a novel narrow width neural network regression method. A novel, well-behaved, and special radial basis function (NRFN) has been developed. We show that the tangent based radial function, a type of NRFN, converges at the same rate as the multiquadric, while having a more favorable condition number that behaves similarly to the multiquadric under a refined mesh size parameter. Furthermore, we prove the method's well-posedness and provide a practical implementation through the use of scikit-learn in parallel high-performance computing environments. Numerical experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness and efficiency.

Pulsar halos are expected to provide key information about how cosmic rays move and spread within the Galaxy. These pulsars that emit strong, directed beams of particles can create long-lived halos within the Galaxy's dense molecular clouds. Although these pulsars represent a small portion of Galactic sources of particle radiation, their unique properties allow scientists to understand cosmic ray behavior on a local scale. This review examines the current state of research on pulsar halos, focusing on the cosmic rays produced and how they spread within the Galaxy's dense regions. It also discusses the potential for future research to connect the pulse-induced particle beams to the cosmic rays within the resulting halos.

This research presents a comprehensive dataset, the RFS Dataset, comprising 1000 precisely labelled frames depicting various weather conditions. The extensive dataset enabled the development of an efficient automated weather conditions detection system, which demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methodologies, including a transfer learning approach. The excellent results achieved suggest that the proposed system has the potential to be integrated into advanced automotive applications, such as rain detection on windshields and roads. The dataset and source code are freely accessible at https://github.com/abdulrahmanalharbi/RFS-Dataset.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as evident from our creation of a Climate Change Index for Europe and the US based on media mentions, whereas economists show relatively little interest as measured by prominent journal publications. Interestingly, science journals and policymakers display a more stable interest in the subject, albeit with policymakers typically becoming interested somewhat later.

Soft grippers are becoming increasingly popular due to their versatility and performance in various applications. Their flexibility and ease of customization allow them to handle objects with complex shapes and high fragility. A significant challenge in soft robotics is controlling the actuation of flexible grippers to ensure reliable performance. In this research, we introduce an innovative approach to controlling a multi-fingered soft gripper using 3D printing and shape-memory alloys as the actuation method. The internal actuation mechanism enables precise control of the gripper's shape through numerical inversion of the actuation strategy, promoting full extension of the gripper. Furthermore, we propose a method for quality assessment of 3D-printed flexible grippers, which considers material properties and quality factors such as surface roughness. This approach facilitates the design and production of high-quality, controllable soft robotic grippers.

One of the most effective algorithms for finding a local minimum in an optimization problem is the Gradient Descent method-Algorithm 11.1 in 84782187. However, this algorithm suffers from two major limitations: 1) It necessitates a preliminary scaling of the problem's variables, a task that can be laborious and cumbersome, especially in complex problems; 2) It necessitates a specific preconditioner for the problem's Hessian matrix to ensure proper convergence, a task that can be arduous due to the lack of a universally applicable method. These challenges can be particularly acute in problems with an excessively large condition number, where the Hessian matrix is significantly not comparable to the identity matrix.

This article presents a novel approach to the Gradient Descent method that overcomes these challenges without requiring a preliminary scaling of the problem's variables or a specific preconditioner. While this method is effective in optimization problems, it may not yield the globally optimal solution as the problem is non-linear.

High-resolution images of the central object in the starless core IRc2 have been obtained using the VLT/VLBI at a 6 cm wavelength, revealing it to be an elongated and symmetric structure. The object exhibits linear features aligned with its major axis, yet lacks a distinct jet. Analysis of the data, combined with prior knowledge, indicates that the central object is likely a young, compact symmetric object and that it may be in the process of being formed or disintegrated. If it is an outflow produced by a protostellar jet, it could be produced by a disc on a binary system that is either at the stage of being formed or has disrupted.

This research focuses on improving survival time predictions for lung cancer patients using a novel deep learning technique. The method integrates text-based clinical information like patient history and drug treatments with visual imaging scans such as CT scans. The target output is the overall survival time of these patients. Notably, our approach combines clinical data processing skills from BERT with a new attention-driven module that fuses scan and treatment data effectively. We validated this model on a publicly available, censored IMVCO-LC dataset, comparing our performance with current survival analysis models and demonstrating the benefits of focusing on FAME tables.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methodologies.

A novel and efficient machine learning approach combined with fast cosmological simulation hardware hardware is introduced as a tool to analyze cosmological density perturbations using quasar spectra. By matching observed spectra with datasets generated by hydrodynamic simulations, this framework enables researchers to extract accurate 1D radial profiles of the intergalactic medium. All necessary data is extracted from SPHIFACE simulations in a quick amount of time. The accuracy and predictive capabilities of this approach are verified through statistical analysis.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to a underlying Lie algebra have finite dimensions. Secondly, we identify the conditions under which tensor products of quasi-finite highest weight modules and U(h)-free modules maintain irreducibility.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions in real-time. This ability
is particularly valuable for entities aiming to grasp customers' perspectives towards their
brand. Our research involves analyzing sentiments expressed by Twitter users in regards to
the 2020 U.S. presidential election. We employed a combination of existing and original
features in our sentiment classification approach. When tested on publicly available data
sets from previous studies, our model surpassed the performance of leading sentiment
analysis tools such as Google's, demonstrating the potential for social media sentiment
analysis to guide individuals and organizations in interpreting the public's emotional responses.

Recent chatbots like HuggingGPT and Google's Builder GPT have garnered significant attention for their ability to incorporate unique characteristics and constraints into open-domain dialogue. Although demonstrating high performance on dialogue tasks with specific features, these systems face a challenge in applying the same features across various domains due to their reliance on domain-specific fine-tuning. In this study, we aim to extend the applicability of persona and safety features to new domains without requiring re-training. We introduce a novel multi-task in-context learning (ICTL) strategy that leverages few-shot examples in large language models to simultaneously satisfy multiple tasks. Our results show that using ICTL not only improves model performance but also enhances its ability to generalize across diverse domains while maintaining consistent application of features.

The binary black hole merger's aftermath leaves a lasting mark on space-time known as gravitational wave memory, and multiple events create a background of residual disturbance known as the stochastic gravitational wave memory background (SGWMB). Researchers found that this phenomenon carries valuable information about the source black holes, including their masses and final velocities, which can't be obtained through gravitational wave amplitude detection. The research also identifies the singularity in the memory background's power spectral density at low frequencies, following a $1/f$ pattern, linking it to the power-law mass spectrum of source black holes. Moreover, simulations using existing LIGO-Virgo data indicate a negligible background level, but future observatories like the space-based LISA and the future Einstein Telescope could significantly improve sensitivity, potentially revealing signs of this phenomenon.

A hypothetical supersymmetry framework offers an extremely attractive explanation for why matter exists in the universe. This theory also predicts the presence of a particle called the axion to solve problems with the amount of matter and the large-scale patterns in the universe. The large mass of a particular particle called a topological axion can be achieved through this topological mechanism. We explore how supersymmetry breaking, which can happen through a first-order phase transition to a zero axion state, might produce axions that pose problems with the amount of matter and large-scale patterns in the universe. The findings from this study can apply to models with both positive and negative amounts of a certain type of energy.

A revolutionary communication system called semantic communication is being developed to efficiently transmit vital meaning at a low cost. To effectively implement this system, an advanced shared semantic space is crucial for seamless communication between users and the network. This paper presents a novel framework that enables cooperative learning of a shared semantic space through a careful selection of cooperative tasks. By leveraging the emergent properties of generated language, specifically designed to fit within the space, the quality of communication can be significantly enhanced. Through the development of a specific language task strategy and a novel reverse translation method to generate meaningful sentences, the proposed framework ensures that a single, universally applicable semantic space can be dynamically created even in dynamic environments. This method also proves more robust and efficient than traditional semantic representations. Detailed simulation results confirm a notable improvement in communication reliability between systems.

The natural language processing challenge of word prediction has received less attention compared to other tasks like text classification and sentiment analysis, primarily due to the absence of extensive, manually created datasets. This research addresses this issue by proposing a novel, fully annotated dataset tailored for English word prediction in real-time messages. Developed from collaboration with language therapists specializing in Alzheimer's treatment, the proposed dataset comprises real-world data collected from patients with Alzheimer's, depicted through the lens of cognitive decline. The research evaluates the efficacy of deep learning algorithms on this novel dataset to showcase their adaptability across diverse NLP applications.

Recent advancements in Session-based recommendation systems have gained significant attention, with notable contributions from embedding-based, collaborative filtering, and collective intelligence methods. However, more recent research has shown that contextual and graph-based techniques can significantly enhance session-based recommendations. A theoretical framework is presented in this paper to categorize and analyze various session-based recommendation methods, with a focus on contextual and graph-based approaches. The proposed framework unifies and categorizes 22 papers from recent conferences and journals, including information about dataset utilization and model structuring. Additionally, this work conducts a practical evaluation on three prominent session-based recommendation datasets and provides a comprehensive review of the contextual and graph-based approach in session-based recommendation systems.

We examine a rigid structure composed of two active Brownian particles that interact in a way that's dependent on their activity levels. The activity of each particle changes randomly and also has a spatial distribution that varies. The configuration of the dimer has a fixed separation, a constant internal bond, and can move about on a two-dimensional surface. Depending on the local activity levels, the dimer exhibits a tendency to move towards or away from areas of higher activity. This movement behavior is influenced by the activity's spatial distribution and also the orientation of the dimer. Monomeric diffusion is used to normalize a range of activity levels that allow for stable configurations. These stable configurations enable the dimer to remain in place, move towards or away from areas of higher activity, or maintain a balance in its activity levels. The steady-state positions of the dimer are found in a way that's independent of how the dimer starts out, and it's determined by a combination of activity levels and area coverage. The activity levels of a stable dimer tend to stay close to a specific value that's similar to the activity level at which particles start to cluster together. The dynamics of the dimer can be better understood in a way that's influenced by activity levels and also the flexibility of an internal bond, and it can be modeled in a way that's based on a simplified version of the dimer's behavior.

A thorough approach is outlined for numerically simulating flow in fractured porous media. The proposed methodology employs the PECB method for flow calculations in a fractured matrix. A key advantage of this approach is its capability to represent both matrix and fracture fields with distinct discretizations, allowing for independent flux computation and conservative interactions between them. To enhance computational efficiency, an optimized global inertia Obedient Bunch Gaussian elimination solver is utilized for solving the resulting linear systems. The effectiveness of this approach in handling complex 3D networks of interconnected domains with varying geometries is demonstrated. Additionally, the method's performance for a real-life case study in heavy oil secondary recovery is examined.

This research focuses on avoiding collisions when multiple autonomous drones operate together in close proximity. We investigate the impact of communication delays and autonomous movement on a message-based collision avoidance system used in drone swarms. Through a case study, we compare this network-dependent approach to a local method that relies on precise predictions of drones' movements. This study utilizes a high-precision simulator to evaluate the effectiveness and scalability of both collision avoidance strategies. Results show that communication-based collision avoidance succeeds in preventing all collisions but, depending on the number of drones, experiences a 2.5 to 5.5 times higher energy consumption and takes up to three times longer to complete tasks than the local method. Notably, the local approach still manages to avoid every collision. This highlights the potential of movement-prediction-based collision avoidance to match the reliability of traditional methods while offering significant improvements in efficiency.

This research explores various spectral characteristics of the Seidel matrix associated with a connected chain graph, demonstrating that $-1$ is always an eigenvalue, while other eigenvalues may have a multiplicity of at most two. We derive the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $-1$, the minimum possible number of eigenvalues exceeding $-1$, eigenfunctions for six of the graph's eigenvalues, and the multiplicity of each of these eigenvalues. Furthermore, we identify the minimum degree of a vertex with an eigenfunction value of zero and present formulae for the multiplicity of the eigenvalues $\pm 1$. We also examine the Seidel spectrum of a special subclass of chain graphs, known as SEE graphs, and determine the minimum possible number of eigenvalues greater than or equal to zero, as well as the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $-1$, for any graph within this subclass.

In our investigation, we focus on a mean-field optimal control issue for stochastic differential equations featuring time-delay, which are influenced by fractional Brownian motion with a Hurst parameter exceeding 0.5. Given the fractional Brownian motion's nature, which defies the criteria for being a Markov process or semi-martingale, we resort to the fractional White noise calculus for analysis. A key characteristic of this scenario is the inability to express the fractional Brownian motion as the derivative of a measure, thereby necessitating a novel approach. Furthermore, the delay component renders the problem non-Markovian, which we tackle by integrating the space-time delay state into the system. Notably, we establish a connection between the value function of the control problem, the delayed state space, and the fractional White noise, which enables the derivation of a necessary first-order stochastic variational equation. Consequently, we establish a necessary and sufficient first-order stochastic optimality condition for the control problem, which encompasses a fractional stochastic calculus of variations framework.

We've developed a unique integration method for a specific expansion of the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator with periodic polynomial diagonal potentials, which self-commutes and interacts properly with its corresponding difference operator. This allows the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator to be factorized into the product of two first-order differential operators. Given that the symbol of the difference operator shares a significant relationship with the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator when treated as a function of the momentum variable, we demonstrated a difference relationship with the symbol. With the non-self-adjoint Dirac operator being essentially a difference operator near the momentum real axis, and assuming the difference operator is marginally首类差分化可逆的, we were able to show that its spectral projections and Riesz projections are smooth across all spaces and remain uniformly bounded there.

RSUs are a vital component in vehicular networks, enabling communication with other vehicles and enhancing connection quality for users. Given their limited resources, it is essential to optimize their placement within an network to maximize performance without incurring excessive costs. Our research focuses on V2I relay utilization in congestion areas where users maintain an link with the network through cones of coverage provided by RSUs. Our goal is to determine the optimal location and number of RSUs necessary to serve a given area effectively. Our optimization model takes into account channel congestion and ensures the quality of service for users while minimizing placement costs. A heuristic algorithm has been developed to solve this problem and in-simulations have shown that our approach effectively balances coverage, load distribution, and cost, outperforming a baseline scheme.

Wikipedia's ultimate goal is to be an authoritative reference on various topics.  Nevertheless, a significant portion of its articles are considered inadequate due to issues with their content and sources.  In an effort to enhance their quality, editors apply a predefined scale that classifies articles by their quality and demands sources for each piece of information within the articles.  In our research, we examined the efficacy of this system by analyzing the responses to requests for sources and sources' overall availability.  We conducted two experiments: a manual review of topics and a system that uses AI to assess sources on various Wikipedia topics.  Our results show that only a small fraction of articles meet high quality standards, and the requests for sources reveal a lack of accessible sources for certain types of information, particularly related to politics, racism, and other sensitive subjects.  AIassisted assessments also found a strong correlation between the difficulty of sourcing and sensitive topics.  We discuss our findings along with the challenges of machinelearning in the context of Wikipedia's articles and verifiability standards.

Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for accelerating the deployment of complex neural networks by transferring their performance to smaller 'student' models using a 'teacher' model. Traditionally, this involved using specialized teacher networks. Our approach leverages several weak, random forest-based models to form a collective 'ensemble' teacher, drawing on an observation that their combined output mirrors close to the training data distribution. These fast and efficient ensemble models can be utilized to deploy lightweight student networks without incurring substantial computational costs, as seen when an image super-resolution task was successfully accomplished with an efficient ResNet. Our method proves effective for both image super-resolution and classification.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collision data acquired at the LHCb experiment with a center-of-mass proton-proton collision energy of 7 and 8 TeV. The $\bar{D}^0$ and $D^0$ mesons in these decays are identified through their respective decay modes $\bar{D}^0\to K^+\pi^-$ and $D^0\to K^+-\pi^+$. The calculated branching fractions for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ are found to be $(1.49\pm0.24\pm0.12\pm0.15)\times10^{-4}$ and $(4.2\pm1.0\pm0.4\pm0.5)\times10^{-4}$ respectively, where the errors are statistical, systematic, based on the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^

The $C^*$-algebra formulation of string theory is explored through topological T-duality. A general class of spaces formed by solutions to Lie group actions is investigated as a method to examine the implications of duality. Specifically, we focus on almost abelian solvmanifolds under coordinate exchange. Our analysis reveals that such exchanges are limited by the structure of the manifold, but when they occur, the resulting space maintains the same mathematical characteristics. As an example, we find that the seven-dimensional solvmanifolds supporting $S^3$-fibrations are closed under the star-exchange operation.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation learning by leveraging expert demonstrations to inform the process. In this study, we thoroughly examine how policy imitation influences off-policy reinforcement learning by developing a theory that captures the policy copywriter's effect on the target policy optimization. Our analysis reveals essential traits a copywriter should possess to facilitate efficient target policy learning. Our research also yields a novel warm-start training approach that leverages the copywriter to accelerate target policy convergence. Our study represents the first comprehensive theoretical analysis of warm-start training in offline reinforcement learning, and our results are empirically validated across a range of scenarios, including simple MDPs, complex games, and real-world robotics tasks.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an optimal performance on average, which significantly reduces communication bandwidth when transmitting information over a channel experiencing severe fading. Our approach involves first determining an optimal metric function for a convolutional code, then analyzing its properties when encoded information is transmitted over a channel and subject to noise, and next developing a function that optimizes the transmission of information from source to receiver in an channel with capacity constraints. A comparative study of various convolutional and polarization-adjusted convolutional codes demonstrates that our proposed metric function yields error-correction performance on par with the best-known rates for PAC codes, while exhibiting a 20% improvement in error-correction performance and a comparable performance with simpler metric functions for conventional codes.

This project outlines a complete ResNet hand gesture tracking system, including the source code, demonstrating its ability to accurately locate hand joints and capture hand posture across a range of movements, all while maintaining a consistent scale. The hand model can also rotate in line with movement, allowing for a clear view of the hand from various angles. The project employs a hand model canonicalization module to keep the hand models consistent and uses a simple, straightforward hand model that can easily adapt to new poses through simple rotations. The code is written in Python 3.6 and leverages the efficiency of AlchemyOne's Hand Canonicalization Module and UlyssesN's ResNet gesture detector for accurate performance.

This study employs a recent method to investigate their respective structure through their star diagrams, for rank 4 Coxeter groups. We examine how this method behaves under rank 4 Chevalley deformations and demonstrate that it yields a fully faithful functor from our deformation into the source category.

A novel, markerless extrinsic calibration system is introduced that relies on real-world video footage to establish a robust link between a stereo camera and robotic end-ef?fs without the necessity for specialized tools or accessories. In contrast to existing approaches that utilize a single camera and a range of fiducial markers, our method utilizes a dual-camera setup and a range of accessible objects like a computer screen. A convolutional neural network is employed to identify a textured object in each camera's field of view, with a 3D reconstruction algorithm generating a sparse point cloud from the two images. By training a single shared network on a diverse set of objects, our system achieves a substantial reduction in outside equipment and fiducial markers required for calibration. Through extensive experiments involving a randomly selected robotic hand, varying optical configurations, and different types of reference objects, our system demonstrates substantial improvements in calibration precision, surpassing existing techniques that rely on a single camera and a range of fiducial markers by a factor of three.

A new model is introduced to describe treatment interference in units, 
where the response is influenced solely by its treatment status and neighboring units' assignments, 
with influence extending up to a certain radius of interaction. This model combines 
key aspects of independence and spatial treatment interference. We conduct a theoretical 
analysis of several UCB and Thompson sampling algorithms under the assumed interdependence 
structure, showing that they achieve deterministically $\epsilon$-admissible treatment 
assignments with high probability, $\epsilon$ being the maximum influence between units. 
Furthermore, we modify existing regret bounds that are applicable in the $\epsilon$-adaptive 
setting. This is accomplished by treating the initially influenced period as a warm-up 
phase and treating the subsequent time as starting from an $\epsilon$-admissible state. 
Numerical simulations demonstrate that this approach yields considerable improvements 
over existing regret bounds that are applicable in the independent setting.

The observed weak-lensing patterns in 104,044 COSMOS galaxies from the Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam Near-Infrared Survey are analyzed to calculate the shear bias and its trend with magnitude. These figures are calculated in relation to an estimated 2Mags-based divide in the sources. The calculated shear bias values are $0.0068 \pm 0.0022, 0.0066 \pm 0.0020, 0.0043 \pm 0.0014$ and there's a residual bias of $-0.0032 \pm 0.0012$ post-correction for the latter's sources. It's observed that this bias carries an uncertainty that may counteract the additive bias and has the potential to confound the interpretation of the sigma-eight values in the Subaru cosmology project. The study proposes potential corrective measures to minimize this bias in studies employing $J$-band selected galaxies. The addditive bias and the trend of the multiplicative bias with source magnitude are found to be in line with the findings of the similar analysis in the redshift 2.5-4.5 range. The analysis of the additive bias and multiplicative bias with redshift is deferred for a forthcoming analysis in the study.

For an irrational rotation $x \mapsto x + \alpha$ and a set of real numbers $A$, we denote $N_\alpha^A(n)$ as the count of instances where a sequence of $n$ rotations results in exactly an odd or even number of landings within $A$. Under the assumption that the set $A$ has a specific characteristic, known as regular, and an additional condition regarding its boundary is met, it can be demonstrated that the parity distribution of the resulting counts holds. Conversely, the same assumption provides a sufficient condition for the parity distribution to be established. Furthermore, as an ancillary outcome, the rotation number of a specific type of homeomorphism can be calculated.

We prove that for k-rational singularities of local complete intersections, k-Du Bois classification applies. For hypersurfaces, k-rationality can be determined based on the minimal exponent. Moreover, certain local vanishing properties for k-rational and k-Du Bois singularities have been identified. These properties were also discovered separately by [FL2].

We've observed the appearance of field-induced Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless correlations in a weakly coupled, spin-1/2 Heisenberg material called [Cu(pz)2(2-HOpy)2](PF6)2. Due to a weak interlayer coupling anisotropy in its hexagonal crystal structure, the material exhibits a three-dimensional anti-ferromagnetic ground state that can be represented as a stack of one-dimensional Heisenberg sub-lattices field-aligned. Applying an external magnetic field that anti-parallelly aligns the stacked layers transforms the material into a two-dimensional XY model. As the field applied is increased, we've observed a level crossing, where the ground state transforms into a two-dimensional antiferromagnetic XZY XZZ ordered state. Beyond this point, we've facilitated the emergence of BKT correlations through the suppression of the inter-layer anti-ferromagnetic correlations. Our experimental observations, including the variation of neutron scattering intensities in a star shape and the specific heat and muon spin relaxation results, suggest that the BKT correlations emerge in this anti-ferromagnetic system at an inter-mediate magnetic field of approximately 7.5 T.

Adding three right-handed neutrinos and a dark matter particle to the standard model's fundamental representation leads to a unique set of constraints on their charges. Specifically, anomalies in certain symmetries fix the charges of hidden particles to a small set of integer values. Assuming R-parity as a stabilizing force for hidden particles and that one of the R-parity-violating couplings drives inflation, anomalies either stabilize or produce dark matter. As a result, multiple discrete gauge symmetries arise that can contribute to the neutrino mass spectrum through the see-saw mechanism, given that one hidden R-parity-violating coupling drives inflation while another generates dark matter. A particular region in the model parameter space aligns with Planck data, including the inflationary spectrum and non-deviating Higgs decay width, while predicting discrete gauge boson masses compatible with current experimental limits. Furthermore, predictions for discrete gauge boson masses will vary depending on whether the dark matter mass is较轻 or较重 than the scale of neutrino masses.

This study optimizes the stabilization efficiency for computing $m$ copies of the magic state $|\mathrm{T}\rangle$ through projective units, achieving an improved upper bound of $\lceil \log_2(m+1) \rceil + 2$, which surpasses prior upper limits and lower bounds of $\lceil \log_2(m) \rceil + 1$ and $\lceil \log_2(m+1) \rceil + 1$, respectively,从而解决了一个提出多年的问题. Moreover, the projective units found offer a substantial improvement in classical description length compared to existing units developed by Kleinmann.

This research employs the Tsallis holographic dark energy model in two scenarios: 
(a) when the Hubble time as the IR cutoff is considered and (b) when the cosmic event horizon as the IR cutoff is considered. Utilizing Raychaudhuri's equation, we calculated the equation of state for both situations. Subsequently, we analyzed the behavior of Tsallis holographic dark energy density and its associated equation of state through mathematical and computational methods. We observed that as the value of the Tsallis parameter $\gamma$ deviates more from unity, the equation of state becomes less than $-1$ at present, indicating that the model in scenario (a) cannot accurately describe a real universe. We further analyzed the acceleration or deceleration of both scenarios based on $\gamma$ and found in scenario (b) the present acceleration and deceleration in the past, with two specific transition times. We observed from state parameters and other results that this research identified two physically viable regions for the Tsallis parameter $\gamma$: $1<\gamma<1.045$ and $1.045<\gamma<1.07$. We observed from state parameters and other results that this research identified two regions for the Tsallis parameter $\gamma$ which are physically viable and they confirm each other. This research further studied the energy density evolution of the Tsallis holographic dark energy in two scenarios and compared it with the LCDM and $\phantom{^{\rm

Between January 2020 and December 2020, the LAMOST performed a unique observation, simultaneously acquiring high-quality low-resolution spectra for over 1.3 million stars. Out of these, 537,726 star spectra met our quality standards, with 89.4% having a high signal-to-noise ratio above 10. Our detailed analysis covered stellar properties such as surface gravity, metallicity, and [O/Fe] ratios, achieved through a well-tested pipeline. These characteristics were used for 464,566 G, K, and M type stars. Our results also included effective temperatures for each star based on a temperature line diagram method. The data collected was systematically documented and added to the LAMOST database for public access.

Previous research has suggested the use of SRAM-based TRNGs which leverage process variation for randomness. As a result, these designs are often seen as the outcome of corner case exploitation. To challenge this, our investigation focuses on SRAM's intrinsic entropy sources and the reasons behind their reliance on corner cases. We identify that SRAM's corner case exploitation stems from two main factors: limited supply voltage to amplify the supply voltage trace, and high driving capability to reduce static SRAM cell delay. These two sources of dependence on supply voltage and delay are crucial for these TRNGs to function. However, they are scarce in commercial SRAM, rendering such designs vulnerable to supply voltage and delay evolution. To address this, our proposed challenge-sensing architecture incorporates an on-die delay generator balancing the SRAM's delay, decoupling their dependence on each other. We implemented a prototype using TSMC's 55nm CMOS process and demonstrated that our design yields sufficient output quality for real-world applications, surpassing the current SRAM-based design's performance.

A pioneering electronic device with the capability to resist change, a molecular assembly, is studied, which is composed of a very small number of atoms. Through simulations based on first-principles calculations, the impact of various elements on this device's functionality - including a gate electrode, a resistive layer, and a bottom electrode - on its resistive switching properties has been assessed. Utilizing gates made of different materials enables control over the electric field to influence the size and charge of the resistive layer. Both the top and bottom electrodes can influence the initial state of the device and its ability to switch to a low-resistance state. Furthermore, gates and bottom electrodes serve as means to fine-tune the high-resistance threshold voltage. Notably, a assembly this small exhibits a remarkable memory effect and retains its properties even after numerous cycles of switching. Its miniaturized size also makes it suitable for one-molecular quantum computing.

The concept of loop-tree duality has emerged as a promising approach for numerically computing multi-loop scattering amplitudes, offering an attractive alternative to traditional methods. By applying loop-tree duality, the four-loop Sun-Yang integrand has been successfully decomposed into real singularities applicable to space-time dimensions. Here we extend its application to complex space-time for a shifted external momentum configuration. After calculating world-sheet diagrams for specific topology and dimension, a by-hand reduction was performed and the result compared with the unitary reduction using a public library. Notably, the computed integrands for two topologies demonstrated a significant speedup of up to a factor of ten.

This paper aims to provide a direct and straightforward proof of a specific eigenfunction expansion formula for one-dimensional quantum walks with two possible states, similar to analogous work done on Sturm-Liouville operators by renowned mathematicians. A related theory involving the CMV matrix already addressed this topic, yet our approach is unique as it focuses specifically on the mentioned quantum walks and also yields valuable properties of Green functions. These properties enable us to derive a precise formula for a positive-matrix-valued measure, ultimately allowing for a direct computation of the spectral measure in a particular model known as the two-phase model.

This study examines the composition of hybrid stars formed by neutrons, protons, and various other particles. The analysis combines the Sigma-omega-rho model for a specific nuclear phase with two distinct quark phase models, and incorporates a multiple-stage phase transition. The model-predicted mass range for hybrid stars is between 0.79 and 1.01 $M_{\odot }$. Given that a massive neutron star named PSR J0044+1721 has a mass range of 2.1$^{+0:31}_{-0.43}M_{\odot}$, our research indicates that the phase transition in both neutrons and neutrons is mostly complete or completely. The mass range of hybrid stars in hybrid stars is directly related to the density at which the phase transition occurs. If a hybrid star more massive than the hybrid star is discovered in the future, it will provide a lower limit for the density at which the phase transition occurs.

The introduction of $q$-deformation into optomechanical systems reveals opportunities to amplify non-traditional optical phenomena. Through $q$-deformed beam splitters and amplifiers, we demonstrate how choosing an appropriate $q$-deformation parameter can enhance the system's sensitivity to minute changes. Furthermore, our analysis of optomechanical models incorporating $q$-deformed operators indicates that $q$-deformation leads to a first-order phase transition with hysteresis, quenching of fluctuation growth, and delayed onset of steady states. In addition, $q$-deformation amplifies the system's response to external signals, potentially heightening its sensing capabilities. Our findings suggest that $q$-deformation offers a valuable framework for exploring novel optical phenomena and improving the performance of optomechanical systems.

In a previous study, I developed a model where the Two-Rotors Model's negative scissors states, consisting of two-sided classical bodies, exhibited 1 |K| = 1; 0 components and negative space parity. Building on this work, I explored reflections across a plane perpendicular to the rotation axes in a broader context, introducing R-reflected states as combinations of particles and antiparticles with swapped quantum numbers. When this reflection operation is applied to the rotation axes, R-negative states, similar to matter-antimatter pairings, are formed. Within these R-negative states, the rotation axes swap directions upon reflection, creating a distinct characteristic. This section demonstrates R-negative properties specifically for negative scissors states, confirming their body-like structure through an explicit calculation that involves swapping the rotation axes and their associated angles. The calculation also shows that the r-function, representing an internal coordinate's wave function, remains unchanged under this transformation, a feature achievable solely in three-dimensional space.

The properties of thin films made from metallic transition-metal oxides can be significantly different from their bulk forms. In this study, we investigate how an interface between a substrate and a functional material impacts the properties of these films. We focused on a very thin film of strontium titanate, specifically one that is right at the threshold of becoming a superconductor when it's in its normal state. We used a technique that combines x-ray scattering with precise control over the sample's orientation to learn more about the electronic and atomic structure of the film. We discovered that the film becomes entirely epitaxial, meaning its atomic structure perfectly matches that of the underlying substrate, as soon as it reaches a certain thickness. This is a crucial factor in determining the film's unique properties and opens the door for precise control over its superconducting critical temperature through precise control over its thickness.

The occurrence of diffusion "anomalous" rather than standard, has been observed in many areas of science and technology. In a 2002 study, Metzler and Weisskopf demonstrated that a linear combination of two normally diffusing substances can exhibit anomalous diffusion, even if individual Fick diffusion processes are involved. The nature of this analogy, primarily mathematical, has hindered broader applications of this method in various fields of science and technology. We reevaluate this phenomenon, explaining it as a consequence of measurement uncertainty inherent to tracking multiple particles simultaneously, a consequence also seen when measuring individual particles. The notion of uncoupling particles, as exemplified by tracing numbered particles of distinct masses, has significant practical implications for simulating particles with uncertain positions, a scenario prevalent in techniques like particle beam propagation and Navier-Stokes equations solving. Moreover, introducing noise or coupling these particles can also result in anomalous diffusion.

This study investigates the effects of information dissemination on cryptocurrency trading networks. Unlike prior research that relied on pairwise correlations, this work examines how numerous information sources impact cryptocurrency stability. A novel network model is introduced, focusing on stable coins and their role in the cryptocurrency ecosystem. The analysis reveals that networks formed through high-order statistical dependencies differ significantly from those based on pairwise relationships. The research highlights the existence of a prominent node representing a stable coin within these networks. The findings suggest that considering high-order dependencies is essential for understanding cryptocurrency behavior and predicting their future stability.

The formation of particles from trace gases is a crucial process that contributes to cloud development by generating the necessary cloud condensation nuclei at levels sufficient to support multiple cloud types. We will examine the effectiveness of the Pleas 2008 formulation, which accurately models particle formation-new particle dynamics-across various trace gases including sulfur, nitrogen, and organic species. Cloud parameterizations will be compared with observations from diverse sources, including ground-based measurements, aircraft surveys, and model simulations, highlighting their global implications.

We introduce and investigate the concept of a compact perception pair, a novel idea that pairs sensors with their input spaces to model systems with potentially unbounded states. A perception pair is considered compact if it can be transformed into a totally bounded measurement space through a continuous function. A perception pair is compact if and only if it can be continuously mapped onto a finite perception pair. We also explore the relationship between compact perception pairs and different classes of functions, including those with continuous perception evaluation and continuous barycentric perception evaluation. Additionally, we introduce the concept of thin sets in the context of perception pairs and demonstrate its relevance to studying compactness through the use of thin closure as a crucial tool for characterizing compact perception pairs with unique minimal balls.

The way solids respond to gravity is well established through gravitational deformation and density changes. However, the effect of gravity on electronic transport is not well understood. Recent research suggests that the gravitational potential can cause electronic currents to flow perpendicular to the direction of the gravity vector. To gain a deeper understanding of this effect, researchers measured the horizontal flow of electrons and the density currents caused by gravity within an aluminum alloy microcantilever that was only a couple of atomic layers thick. The experiment involved orienting the microcantilever at different angles to measure the horizontal flow of electrons and the density currents caused by gravity when the device was positioned vertically. The results showed horizontal flows of electrons and the density currents caused by gravity within the range of $10^{-12}$ to $10^{-9}$ times the vertical flow of electrons and the respective density current. These results indicate the existence of a relativistic connection between the gravitational field and electric field that affects the flow of electrons within solid-state systems.

In various machine learning scenarios, simpler models are generally preferred to their more complex counterparts, and controlling model complexity, also known as regularization, is a crucial aspect, although its full understanding remains incomplete, especially in deep learning where models exhibit exceptional performance, and compact versions are often overlooked, and dimensionality reduction techniques have not been thoroughly applied during the training phase, and our research introduces a novel approach where geometric properties of trained models are used as a complexity penalty and studied in an information-theoretic framework, and we define a concept of geometric complexity that evaluates the separation between trained models and test data and proposes minimizing this complexity to achieve the best results, and we provide examples of effective simplicity methods, such as those based on truncation and regularization, and our study is an empirical investigation, and we found that geometric complexity decreases with training and that geometric regularization yields similar outcomes to traditional methods, and we provide theoretical justification for the effectiveness of this approach.

A new approach for directly extracting the Wilson coefficients of rare $b\to s$ processes is developed using $B^0\to K^{*0}\mu^+\mu^-$ decays within an unbinned maximum likelihood framework. This novel method outperforms traditional Wilson coefficient determination by utilizing all available data and accounting for experimental correlations without segmentation into $q^2$ bins. Simulation results confirm the improved sensitivity and potential to leverage the complete Run 1 and 2 LHCb dataset in practice.

Automated essay scoring has been long explored in Natural Language Processing with notable advances in neural network-based approaches. Notably, using pre-trained models, such as BERT and RoBERTa, with fine-tuning techniques has led to superior performance in automated scoring tasks. Despite significant progress, notable discrepancies persist between models and systems from the TACL 2019 benchmark. This study investigates the pre-training objective's impact on scoring differences and examines the correlation between models' divergence in embedding space and scoring discrepancies. The results indicate that embedding space distance correlates linearly with scoring discrepancies, suggesting that discrepancies in pre-training objectives contribute to variations in scoring performance. The authors propose that further research should investigate the influence of dataset characteristics on scoring discrepancies.

Given a simplicial complex defining a tensor's marginalizations, we restrict them to rank one, an idea developed from Kirkup and Sullivant's work on toric models. We delve into the toric ideals arising from such marginal independence models, with a specific focus on models for random graphs and matroids' independent set polytopes. We also explore numerical methods for parameter estimation through both Euclidean distance and maximum likelihood techniques and establish a database for small model examples.

A higher education system is crucial to maintain social mobility across different generations, yet political changes in the United States may be hindering mobility for individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. In this study, we utilize a model of intergenerational mobility to assess the social returns related to expansions or contractions in college availability. Our analysis reveals that reductions in social mobility can result in substantial long-term social losses, exceeding $100 billion after ten years. Based on this, we utilize our model to derive a key social return metric for college enrollment variations, which accounts for the intertemporal social impacts. Notably, this model indicates that the calculated social return for a typical college major can reach as high as 43.3 times the private return after ten years.

The symmetry of wavefunctions under parity for particles of arbitrary spin is responsible for determining the wavefunction exchange statistics when the particles are permuted. According to non-relativistic quantum mechanics, the properties of angular momentum alone account for the sign factor resulting from the particle permutation, which relates spin to particle exchange statistics in this context.

We introduce an upgraded RingCT protocol that supports stealth addresses in conjunction with Delegated Proof of Stake, specifically for decentralized cryptocurrencies. The DELEGATED_RINGCT protocol is a technical solution requiring no changes to ringCT or DPOS, making it a compatible add-on for existing systems, and we highlight Monero's compatibility with this add-on. Delegation allows trust-mined coins to maintain privacy while significantly reducing key sizes, thereby optimizing storage and transaction costs for delegated addresses. For example, a delegation depth of three results in a public key that's just one hash larger than a standard DPOS public key. Achieving this compactness relies on the innovative use of Chaum's blinding factor recursion scheme.

If more specific subclasses of linear systems can be solved in near-logarithmic space, this capability can be applied to solve a broader range of linear systems within a similar space complexity. Our findings build on work by Kyng and Zhang who previously made similar discoveries in terms of time complexity, utilizing reductions between approximate solvers; our own proof demonstrates that these reductions can be implemented using near-optimal space complexity, within an additive \(O(\log n)) factor.

This paper describes an investigation into the production of three massive gauge bosions alongside one additional jet at the LHC, using data collected at a 13 TeV energy level. The investigation involved analysis of the proton-proton collision data, which resulted in the observation of data that either matched or exceeded the levels predicted by the standard model. Notably, the data revealed no signs of a beyond standard model process, and the findings reached a significance level of 2.7 standard deviations. Through quantitative analysis, the sensitivity of the study was determined to be the capacity to reject hypothetical cross sections of five separate production channels by 95% confidence level, with values ranging between 0.61 and 0.74 pb.

Previous foundational Hebrew NLP tasks have heavily relied on English-based
annotation traditions and tools, creating significant challenges in terms of time
consumption, resource allocation, and technical feasibility. To overcome these
limitations, a new system called HErule Hebrew has been proposed, an AI-powered
AI assistant specifically trained on and proficient in the nuances of the Hebrew
language. HErule serves multiple functions, including streamlining the process of
creating annotation guidelines, drafting the content of such guidelines, making
localizations of existing English guidelines, creating annotation tools, and
facilitating the remote annotation process.

We maintain fixed $p \in [1,\infty)$ and $K \in (0,\infty)$ and a probability measure $\mu$ on a product of countably many balls with diameters bounded by 1. Given a function set $\mathcal{F}$ consisting of $\mu$-bounded components with $\mu$-variation not exceeding $K$, its elements are real-valued functions defined on a potentially infinite measure space $\Omega$. Denoting $\mathcal{I}_p(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mu)$ as a class of functions defined on $\Omega$ whose values lie in the $\ell_p$-sum of $\mathcal{F}$ and are bounded pointwise by $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} |f(x)| \leq \left(\sum_{f \in \mathcal{F}} |f(x)|^p\right)^{1/p}$, with $\ell_p$-norm given by $\|f\|_{\ell_p(\mu)}^p = \sum_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p$, then:

1) There exists a linear operator $\Phi$ defined on $\Omega$ and taking values in a space $\Phi(\Omega)$ and defined on $\mathcal{F}$ and taking values in an set $\Phi(\mathcal{F})$ with the following properties

In recent years, advancements in artificial neural networks have led to substantial
progress across various fields. Concurrently, researchers are placing greater emphasis
on developing AI systems that adhere to ethical guidelines and function reliably
throughout their entire lifespan. A major obstacle arises from the discrepancy between
the narrow expertise of traditional AI models, which excel at individual tasks but suffer
from limited knowledge and a lack of adaptability to new, related tasks. Furthermore,
these models tend to disregard previously acquired information when learning new data,
a phenomenon referred to as catastrophic forgetting. To circumvent this issue,
several attempts have been made to create flexible neural networks capable of resolving
the challenge of continual learning. A notable approach involves leveraging external
memory mechanisms to store crucial data for individual tasks, allowing the network to
access this information when needed. This paper explores such memory-based methods,
focusing on specific techniques, including the design of memory units, strategies for
populating them, and methods of access, while also discussing open problems and
future directions in this field.
