Let $\mathcal{R}_{<}$ be a strict order on a non-zero ring $\mathcal{R}$ of size $n \times n$ consisting of lower triangular matrices over an abelian group $\mathcal{A}$. By extending $\mathcal{R}_{<}$ to a maximal form $\mathcal{R}^{*}$, it is possible to establish a direct relationship between elements of an affine plane of dimension $r+1$ and the non-free cyclic submodules of $\mathcal{R}^{*}$ over a specific ring of size $n \times n$ consisting of lower triangular matrices over the field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$. Additionally, $\mathcal{R}^{*}$ can be mapped to a direct product of $\mathcal{M}_{p}(\mathbb{F}_{p})$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{p}^{(k)}$, where $\mathbb{Z}_{p}^{(k)}$ represents the additive group of integers modulo $p$ of size $k$, and this relationship enables the calculation of $\mathcal{R}^{*}$'s points.

In a 1986 paper in J. Symbolic Logic, Pawlikowski demonstrated that under specific conditions regarding Cohen and random reals, certain model properties can be inferred. This is reflected in theorems stating that if a model contains only Cohen or random reals, its first-order theory can be fully captured in a specific logical system. This concept is generalized to any real-valued measurable cardinal, revealing multiple instances of consistency within the specified logical framework.

A key concept in data-driven decision-making for dynamic environments is the construction of reliable treatment patterns from observational data, known as the off-policy learning problem. The pessimism principle has proven effective in developing safe learning methods, although most existing approaches assume a fixed set of treatment patterns in advance. This research introduces a novel pessimism-based learning method that dynamically constructs treatment patterns by clustering, utilizing the Hoeffding decomposition to efficiently estimate residual values. Experimental results confirm the proposed method's ability to construct both off-policy learning and risk-control patterns of treatment patterns.

Dualities between subcategories of finitely generated modules over Artin algebras can be defined by the relationship to Wakamatsu tilting bimodules, with specific cases yielding known dualities. When restricting these relationships to subcategories of finitely generated modules with particular dimensions, both tilting and restricted tilting scenarios are possible. The text explores and examples illustrate how certain known dualities can be framed in the context of Wakamatsu tilting. It explores how these relationships can be further restricted to yield restricted dualities with tilting properties. Furthermore, the text examines andrelations between Wakamatsu tilting C-dimension and its special case of Cohen--Macaulay C-dimension.

A proposed Witting configuration, with a different complexity of 40 rays, could reformulate the Penrose model for spin-3/2 systems based on a dodecahedron's geometry, to study quantum mechanics' nonlocality and contextuality. An alternative setup using 120 states is examined in this work. Despite their different sizes, both arrangements are linked to a shared 8D root system scaled by 10, which can be connected to the $E_8$ Lie algebra. An 11D setup using 1320 pure states is also proposed, derived from the $E_8$ root system. Their geometry is defined through high-dimensional projections, but their associated graph structures lack complete correspondence. Initial assessments of their information content are presented along with discussions on the feasibility of 40-ray and 120-ray setups' construction.

In a flat band superconductor, bosonic modes can propagate freely due to pairing induced by a negative pairing potential. It is found that in one- and two-dimensional systems with spin-degenerate bands, pairing the highest energy state results in a complete quenching of electron motion. Conversely, pairing lower-lying states allows for the coexistence of superconductivity and dynamic electron behavior. The resulting dynamic process gives rise to an energy gap for the single-particle excitation, with the magnitude of this energy gap being determined by the distribution of the lower-band wave functions.

The Gaussian distribution is uniquely determined by the distribution of a linear combination and a power function of independent identically distributed random variables. We identify the a-adic solenoids for which this relationship holds, effectively proving a generalized Polya theorem. This proof relies on solving a functional equation for a specific class of functions associated with the character group of the a-adic solenoid.

Presence-absence data is prevalent in scientific research and engineering fields. Although statistical models for this type of data have been developed over the past century, they often rely on stringent conditions that may not always be met in practice. A new approach for analyzing presence-absence data based on the multivariate spatial Poisson process will be presented here. This approach results in a flexible framework that accommodates various real-world scenarios and boasts relaxed assumptions compared to existing alternatives. The associated regression model can be effectively addressed through various methods, one of which is fully specified Bayesian estimation. Simulation studies and an application based on ecological data from the Azores islands will be used to demonstrate the approach.

In recent years, the performance of salient object detection has seen significant improvement with the integration of multi-scale feature fusion and the reorganization of channel spatial rearrangement. Nevertheless, current reorganization methods primarily focus on long-range dependencies within individual input branches, with the inter-branch short-range dependencies often being disregarded in the fusion process. Furthermore, existing approaches offer a uniform level of detail in the feature maps, which may not be adaptable to objects of varying sizes. To address these issues, we propose a novel reorganization method that integrates a cross-attention context extraction salient object detection. Specifically, our approach leverages the depth features from both the PBP PAM and FCBM feature branches to encode the mean features of the cross-branch short-range depth maps. Subsequently, the rich information from the FCBM branch is decoded into the PBP PAM branch's query feature map through a cross-attention context extraction module to enhance the PBP PAM's PAM feature map. Notably, the cross-attention mechanism enables the model to adapt to different feature map sizes, thus achieving better results for small-scale objects. Comprehensive evaluations on the ECSD and PDP datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method compared to existing methods.

The UM-IU@LING system for the 2019 SemEval OffensEval Task is the subject of this research, with a goal of identifying and classifying abusive content in Twitter posts and tweets as either general offensiveness or more specific forms, such as profanity, racist, and hostile language. To achieve this objective, the team adapted an existing BERT model and modified it by replacing the original token-level classification with a word-piece level approach. They then manually selected the most effective parameters and fine-tuned a classifier using this customized model on the provided training data.

A number, when written in binary form, is said to be a palindrome, if the order of its binary digits symmetricalsly matches its reverse. A newly created graph structure, known as the binary palindrome graph, connects two vertices, a and b, when the binary addition of a and b results in a binary palindrome. Researchers investigated the property of cliques within this graph, specifically the largest subgroups of vertices, all of which, when paired, result in a binary palindrome sum. The goal of their study was to determine the largest groups of vertices with this characteristic, denoted as cliques of size k, within the graph applied to numbers from 0 to n. Notably, the researchers found that the size of these cliques continually grow as numbers increase, proving that the clique at number k is strictly less than the clique at k+1. Furthermore, the researchers supplied a program to automatically identify the initial values of numbers that result in a new size of cliques. By the program, the researchers discovered the size of cliques at number 1, 2, 3, ..., 21, with the largest group of vertices, all of which, when paired, result in a binary palindrome sum, found to be 1, 024, 404.

When X-ray beams consist of multiple energy levels, commonly seen in both traditional polyenergetic X-ray tube and emerging spectral CT techniques, material inhomogeneity can lead to various image distortions such as beam hardening, scattering, and cross-talk. These issues complicate image interpretation and make accurate 3D object segmentation and measurements difficult. Although a basic model can account for these effects and express them in terms of linear attenuation, more sophisticated models are required as X-ray energies diverge. This research introduces a method to quantify and correct a more complex polyenergetic X-ray model by designing and testing a dedicated experimental setup on a spectral CT scanner. Two models are applied to correct beam hardening and cross-talk effects: a fundamental three-material model and an advanced model based on measured mass energy attenuation coefficients. The proposed models demonstrate a significant reduction in residual values to less than 2% of the full energy range, effectively eliminating the effects.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) with limited resources is a complex challenge, largely due to the scarcity of labeled data required to train machine learning models. One specific issue arises with historical documents, which often lack training data and must be trained from scratch. A notable example is Old German Handwriting (OGD), which presents additional difficulties. To address these problems, researchers have developed transfer learning techniques that leverage knowledge from well-resourced systems and adapt them to under-resourced systems like OGD. In this study, investigators put the performance of three transfer learning methods to the test on OGD, comparing them to a strong baseline, before exploring the effects of adapting these systems by either increasing the training data or employing domain-specific knowledge.

We have evaluated several observable parameters in closed-shell even-even atomic nuclei utilizing an ab initio calculation framework based on the no-core shell model with auxiliary-field diffusion Monte Carlo, which enables precise determination of many-body wave functions. Our method involves variational and projected quantum Monte Carlo techniques to compute binding energies and root-mean-square radii in nuclei with zero or 2 units of angular momentum, respectively. By focusing on the $^{16}$O nucleus under various spectral truncations defined by the maximum single-particle energy and angular momentum, we found that a specific cutoff yields accurate results comparable to experimental data. Additionally, we obtained precise binding energies and radii for a range of closed-shell even-even carbon and oxygen isotopes and discovered a notable discrepancy between our calculated charges and masses, which however diminishes as we move towards an adjacent nucleus.

We invite undergraduate students and early graduate students to an educational introduction to one-dimensional topological phases, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. This will include discussions on entanglement using the correlator method and von Neumann density matrix, as well as geometric phase, polarization, and transport characteristics, all with consideration of electron-electron interactions. Hands-on numerical experiments guided by publicly available codes are used to convey the value of using topological toy models for exploring new concepts in quantum electronics.

This study examines the compactness of composition operators within Bergman spaces associated with certain bounded, convex domains in complex n-dimensional space containing non-trivial analytic circles in the complex n-dimensional space. Consequently, this characterizes compactness of the composition operator with a continuous symbol on Bergman spaces within strictly convex, bounded pseudoconvex domains within C^n.

We develop a continuous formulation for computing gravitational amplitudes in AdS$_5$ and dS$_5$ spaces. Drawing from the successful application of the LHC, we transform discrete calculations of multi-particle final states into a seamless framework. We derive a general prescription for finite and regularizing expressions of graviton amplitudes. Furthermore, we confirm that this formulation yields expected results in the flat limit and as the number of particles $N$ increases, with this approach also simplifying the determination of the leading large-$N$ behavior.

High-performance computing has gained prominence over the past few decades due to its ability to accelerate the development of scientific and engineering applications that are challenging to address on a single computer. As high-performance applications continue to evolve and their demands increase, the need for efficient and reliable execution frameworks grows paramount. This study introduces a novel Python-based system called Single-Method Multiple-Objects, or SMMO, designed to simplify the management of executable files through a unified interface while supporting diverse object types with common common functions and attributes. SMMO's flexibility and object-oriented design enable researchers to develop custom objects tailored to their requirements, be it batch submission or containerized objects. SMMO's comprehensive documentation and modular design facilitate easy learning and integration into existing projects.

We introduce family universal U(1)X models incorporating three right-handed neutrinos, by defining U(1)X as a composite of SO(10) U(1)Y and U(1)χ gauge symmetries. To incorporate quantum gravity effects, we propose the introduction of a Dirac fermion χ as a dark matter candidate that's a matter candidate is a violation of L_e - L_μ.

A specific measurement technique is developed to determine the mechanical characteristics of straw tubes, including their Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and outer diameter, by simply observing their resonance frequency when bent at the first and second harmonic modes. The Poisson's ratio values obtained validate the structural integrity of the straw tubes under typical operating conditions, given that the maximum stress applied during the measurement does not exceed the threshold that could cause damage to the tubes. The introduced methodology is presented as a useful addition to existing production quality checks for straw tubes, offering an advantage of requiring minimal equipment, which can be utilized with a basic setup consisting of a vibration exciter and basic audio analysis tools, allowing for cost-effective implementation, especially in institutions where specialized equipment, like laser doppler vibrometers, is not easily accessible.

In various fields such as supervised classification and regression, there is a growing interest in developing decision functions that can be fully trusted. To this end, we concentrate on the general decision function case and two key reliability metrics, marginal reliability and the maximum marginal probability. Our main goal is to establish theoretically-backed guidelines for ensuring these metrics meet specified thresholds in training data. Notably, we can be precisely quantificationally conservative when tracing down implications from empirical trust criteria to the decision function performance. Our investigation also considers the more intricate scenario of decision functions based on multiple output predictions.

In a supersolid Bose-Einstein condensate with a spin-orbit coupling, an accelerated impurity atom exhibits oscillations that mirror Bloch oscillations in solid matter, despite causing condensate excitements that give rise to internal phonon modes. However, these oscillations have no impact on the condensate's roton minimum position, thereby preserving its periodic matter wave pattern. Notably, the oscillations fade rapidly due to an inverse roton Rayleigh instability. The study's findings open up possibilities for exploring the intricate behavior of supersolid condensates when subjected to external acceleration or gravitational forces, while also revealing a new mechanism for detecting the spin-orbit coupling in these complex atom-matter systems.

We introduce and study a new class of generalized quadrangles, denoted as $\mathcal{Q}(C)$, which are derived from specific constant weight codes, Delsue quadrangles, and can be extended to a residual quadrangle. Additionally, we establish conditions for obtaining a distance 4 code through group action on a binary code.

Located at the heart of the Milky Way lies the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ), a region encompassing the Galactic center and a area with a range of radii from a few parsecs to a few hundred parsecs. Research has shown that within the 100 parsecs radius, a dense gas with a total mass of about 100 solar masses per cube, is characterized by a centrally concentrated density distribution that follows a power of -1.1, as determined by multiple observational and numerical methods. In this study, a detailed analysis of a 3D simulation of gas dynamics in the CMZ is conducted using a recently developed tool called the 3D Gaussian Tool. Applying this tool to simulation data from different angles and sizes reveals a strong alignment with the simulation's inherent parameters. Furthermore, a comparison of the simulated and real observed properties using the 3D Gaussian tool shows a strong match in terms of map density and column density, although a discrepancy arises regarding the presence of a gas hole observed in observations but absent in simulation data when analyzed using the 3D Gaussian density.

Understanding the impact of synchrotron light intensity, expressed as beam brightness, on the experimental data gathered during X-ray absorption near edge spectroscopy (XANES) experiments, has led researchers to develop a theoretical framework to interpret the observed changes in the XANES signal at various fluence levels. This study utilized non-resonant and resonant scanning methods to monitor the beta vanadium in vanadium dioxide samples, observing distinct effects at high fluence levels despite a successful initial data collection process. Furthermore, experiments involving different synchrotron beamlines with varying beam sizes and energy settings showed that the breakdown of traditional XANES mu2 or mu3 rules is a common phenomenon and not solely attributed to the photon flux. It has also been found that the changes in the XANES signal can be partially explained by the shift in vanadium's L3 edge due to beam-induced thermal effects, supported by data from X-ray linear edge spectroscopy (XLES) and room temperature measurements, as well as room for other, as-of-yet unidentified, contributions.

This research presents the development of a fully integrated CMOS temperature sensor in conjunction with a novel sensing scheme in 40-nm CMOS technology, achieving a low power consumption of micro-watts for precise temperature readings. The proposed method reduces the power requirement in proportion to the scaling of supply voltage, enabling its effective utilization in mobile devices and computer systems that employ dynamic voltage and frequency scaling. The temperature sensing circuit consists of a supply-voltage-scaled differential pair, optimized for enhanced power efficiency and performance. By leveraging deep-N-well transistors for enhanced offset modulation and leveraging a 40-nm CMOS process with a high metal count of 9, design objectives of low power and high precision are successfully achieved, demonstrating a power consumption of 12.6 micro-watts over a 0.7-volt operating range, enabling temperature readings within the 300K to 350K range with an accuracy of ±2K.

Quantum entanglement is a fundamental concept in quantum information science and technologies.  Among the various forms of entanglement, polarization entanglement has been the most widely utilized due to its relevance. In this paper, two distinct methods are employed to analyze entanglement, namely density matrices and entanglement measures, with a specific focus to describe entanglement in complex systems such as mixed states and high-dimensional entanglement.

This paper explores the concept of online Euclidean spanners for specific geometric settings, considering different dimensions and distance metrics. It specifically focuses on the case where points arrive and are associated with weights, and investigates how to create geometric structures that maintain efficient distances between these points. 

In a 1D environment using the L_1 metric, where each point has a non-negative weight, the research establishes a minimum threshold of n/4 for the best possible performance of a certain type of geometric structure that maintains (1+ε) distance accuracy, applicable when ε approaches zero. 

Additionally, it is shown that at least 3 is the minimum required efficiency of an online L_1 geometric structure (spanner) algorithm that remains effective regardless of the specific weight distribution for any number of points within a set. 

Furthermore, the creation of at least (1+ε') efficient geometric structure (spanner) algorithms for any small ε' > 0 that remain adaptive to point weights is possible in the (1+ε) geometric structure (spanner) problem for any specific point p within a set S, ensuring that the distance between p and all other points in S is not increased by more than a certain factor. 

Lastly, the research examines the dynamic nature of geometric structure preservation when using an L_1 metric in a two-dimensional environment, where a point with a specific non-negative weight is added or removed from a set, and the effect on a certain type of geometric structure (ε-d

Accurate identification of IoT devices is a critical component of IoT-based security systems, yet existing passive approaches achieve high correctness rates, make little to no profit, and incur unacceptably high costs due to the extensive feature set required for the 64-device classification, which demands approximately 1542 seconds. Our proposed solution combines a multi-task network with active learning to minimize the number of labels needed across the 64 IoT devices, allowing simultaneous extraction of information from multiple sources to reduce costs and increase profitability. By integrating active learning, the model selects the most instructive data samples to reduce training expenses. Our approach successfully classifies 99.5% of 64 IoT devices using as few as just under 2000 packets, reducing the data load by over 98% compared to traditional deep learning methods.

This study explores G\"odel modal logies based on Kleene's third-valued semantics. G\"odel modal logics can be regarded as an extension of intuitionistic modal logics, but they treat truth values differently - with the third value being neither strictly false nor strictly true, but neither simultaneously. This leads to the observation that in G\"odel modal logics, a formula's instance can be neither strictly true nor strictly false, but rather has an "undefined" truth value. The study offers an axiomatic description of G\"odel modal logics with specified truth table constraints. The resulting framework can be seen as a subset of full-valued G\"odel modal logics, which are defined by their valuations into the [0,1] interval. Furthermore, the study establishes that certain complex formulas are decidable given an n-variable constraint. Specifically, it determines whether a formula is effectively equivalent to a simpler, basic formula with the same modal operators. The study also provides a key unification theorem for G\"odel modal logics. The theorem states that two carefully constructed formulas are considered logically equivalent within a specific G\"odel modal logic if and only if a more complex formula is also considered logically equivalent to a simpler, basic formula within a related logic. This theorem can be derived by adapting a method for full-valued G\"odel modal logics, which in turn relies on a more fundamental theorem for intuitionistic logic. This research presents a novel and straightforward technique for word-alignment that leverages bilingual information from external sources like machine translation platforms. We demonstrate that a model with limited parameters can achieve performance comparable to GIZA++ when trained on a relatively small dataset. Furthermore, in terms of alignment metrics, our approach outperforms GIZA++ when utilizing sources of bilingual information that are distinct from those used in training. Finally, this method exhibits a high degree of flexibility in terms of training data requirements.

We suggest an asynchronous algorithm to solve Nash equilibrium problems by iteratively decomposing the mixed strategies. This methodology is heavily grounded in monotone operator theory, utilizing warped resolvents for handling a combination of nonsmooth and smooth functions involved in strategy mixtures.

We have developed a code to solve the radiation hydrodynamics equations in an in-out flowing scenario. This numerical method is applied to a theorized primordial black hole scenario, where primeval holographic fluid is drawn into the black hole and pushed outward in a symmetric manner. When solving the hydrodynamics equations, we consider the fluid's local temperature and fluid velocity, as well as their relative movement, for a fluid that is pushed outward at a speed of v_out/M = 0.3. This code is written in Fortran95 and can be utilized to study the interaction between the primordial black hole and the surrounding holographic fluid.

We conducted an in-depth study of wedge-shaped monodisperse molecules, which exhibited rich liquid crystalline behavior. When the packing density did not exceed 0.5, the system exhibited typical liquid crystalline phases, namely, near a smectic A phase with tilted layers, and a hexatic phase. However, at higher packing densities, it showed a complex transition to a chiral columnar lattice with a triangular 2D unit cell. Extensive studies, including entropy calculations and perturbation theory analyses, were performed. Our results indicated that entropy dominated the system's characteristics, with the complex chiral lattice lowering entropy compared to a hypothetical non-chiral one. Monte Carlo simulations were used to verify the stability of the chiral phase and its structural and orientational properties.

For $0<\nu<1$, we analyze positive definiteness of zonal functions on the unit sphere, relating them to coefficients in their Gegenbauer polynomial series expansions. We confirm the older theorem by Wendland and also examine how it interacts with Bochner's theorem in specific cases, specifically when $d=3$ and when $d\in\{5,7,9\}$.

This work builds upon existing involution architectures, incorporating a novel connection type aimed at enhancing image processing capabilities. Unlike standard convolutions, cross-channel connections operate across images of differing resolutions, enabling the model to generate contextual information and enable higher-level reasoning. To enable training without paired images, we adopt the unpaired monocular depth estimation approach and leverage an unsupervised scene flow estimation task to provide additional context for the network. By training the model on a diverse range of datasets, we achieve a flexible and highly performing model excelling in both depth estimation and scene flow prediction. Furthermore, our model demonstrates exceptional performance in right-angle rotation tasks and can reconstruct 3D surfaces from 2D images. The cross-channel mechanism also facilitates efficient image super-resolution, enabling the model to translate low-resolution images into high-resolution format. The proposed model demonstrates the effectiveness of involution-based architectures in handling complex image processing scenarios and has the potential for broader application across a range of tasks.

The flow of complex liquids is significantly influenced by surface roughness, especially at interfaces. Through a combined approach using stress measurements and optical analysis, we investigated the effects of different surface roughness on dry polymers. Our research reveals the existence of three distinct friction modes, each arising from a specific friction mechanism. Furthermore, we have developed a roughness parameter that indicates a transition between the first two friction regimes. Notably, we have demonstrated a relationship between this parameter and the liquid's relaxation time.

This report details our methods and outcomes in response to the 2019 Challenge for the Image Analysis Challenge for Skin Cancer using Deep Learning run by the University of Basque and collaborated with Pathology at Donostia. The objective of this project is to utilize deep learning techniques to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of diagnosing skin cancers such as BCC and melanoma. Our innovative approach employs a modified and pre-trained CNN model, fine-tuned with the provided dataset and augmented with synthetic data to achieve a final accuracy of 94.8% for the melanoma task and an impressive top-1 accuracy of 95.42 with 5 correct predictions out of 10 for the BCC task in the two-stage evaluation.

We carried out a high-resolution ARPES study on sodium and found that the observed enhancement of its electronic mass is slightly less than expected from earlier research. These findings amplify the need for theoretical models more advanced than the random phase approximation. Contrary to the hypothesis suggesting significant acceleration of the carriers due to their interaction with spin fluctuations, our results do not support this theory. Additionally, a comparison with previous electron loss data indicates that sodium's mass enhancement due to dipole-type electron-hole interactions is substantially lower than that of its magnetic counterpart, vanadium.

Building on a novel theoretical framework, microstate physics, we offer a macroscopic interpretation of thermo-informational phenomena, which reconciles the apparent contradictions between classical physics and modern micro-macro connections. This construction yields a rigorous macroscopic theory that explains the irreversible behavior of physical systems. Notably, the use of information's stochastic nature clarifies the limitations of determinism, as seen in the evolution of free energy and free enthalpy. Conversely, the first principle for calculating microwork is presented, demonstrating that it generally exhibits non-zero, non-averaged values during non-equilibrium processes such as free expansion, with a statistically prevalent negative value indicative of energy release.

This passage provides an in-depth, explicit calculation for the weights of Kontsevich graphs that emerge from connections and curvatures within a symplectic manifold framework, specifically focusing on globalization. We'll demonstrate how curvature graph weights can be explicitly defined through a hypergeometric function and an even simpler expression that combines it with a formula for the underlying connection graph. Notably, we examine a cotangent bundle case, leading to a substantial simplification of the curvature expression.

We explore solitary waves known as "nanoptera," which exhibit exponential tails coupled with oscillating algebraic patterns, through the analysis of a singularly perturbed, conservative, nonlinear elastic chain governed by Hertzian nonlinearities. By comparing the long-term behavior of these waves to solutions of a constant-coefficient linear equation, which better captures their complex tail structures, we demonstrate that localized wave states, sometimes called "breathers," cannot exist in both PT-symmetric and conservative regimes. These nanoptera waves emerge from the resonance of a wave with a wavenumber of zero and the unperturbed spectrum of the underlying linear system, which features a marginal point of geometric multiplicity one but algebraic multiplicity two.

We explore the potential of addressing diverse cosmological initial conditions through a non-geodesic, oscillating inflationary model. Focusing on an example with a single scalar field, our work examines the spectrum of curvature perturbations, de Sitter non-gaussianity, and cosmological cosmic perturbations of large-scale structures. We demonstrate that this model can satisfy the adiabatic vacuum assumption, leading to a power spectrum of curvature perturbations that aligns with observational data, specifically $A_s^{0.05}\approx0.2074$ and $n_s^{0.05}\approx0.9745$. We calculate a non-linear parameter $f_{NL}^{0.05}=-1.1264$, indicating a small, non-zero value, which we interpret as an indirect, signature of the proposed model. We approximate Hubble-crossing using the slow-roll approximation, obtaining a value for the cosmic equation of state consistent with PLANCK data when inflation ends.

Consider a graph of even order G and its complete graph counterpart K_G. A pairing of G refers to a set of edge disjoint cycles that cover all edges of G. When such a pairing consists of just n/2 edge cycles of length two, it forms a pairing-hamiltonian decomposition (PHD). A graph with a pairing-hamiltonian property possesses a PHD. This study examines the PHD in label graphs of permutations, specifically focusing on the ordered configuration graphs OPC(n,k). By determining the maximum value of k for which O(n,k)(n) has the PHD property, we gain insight into the PHD property in family O(n,1), O(n,2), and O(n,3). For the case of O(n,3), we prove that an OPHD exists by constructing a pairing-hamiltonian decomposition.

We carry out a finite-time thermodynamics analysis of wavepacket spreading in a three-state quantum walk. The initial wavepacket is created at the first state with a deterministic probability distribution. The angle of the initial wavepacket, denoted as θ, is found to significantly influence its dynamics. For θ = π/2, the wavepacket remains confined and does not display Fock state localization, unlike scenarios where θ is not π/2 and localized Fock states emerge. A transition from erasure-like behavior to diffusion is observed, where the wavepacket either remains or spreads. Near θ = π/2, the wavepacket exhibits maximum confinement. The team executing the three-state quantum wavepacket is based on a protocol developed through a parabolic potential, realizing the model via a trapped-ion system.

This study delves into self-supervised learning of Visual Transformers (ViT), comparing it to supervised learning of ViT and traditional convolutional networks, all targeting semantic segmentation tasks. To train ViT models effectively without human annotation, self-supervised learning leverages large datasets to derive labels automatically. Our findings reveal that ViT model trained in a self-supervised manner surpasses both convolutional and supervised ViT models, showcasing its potential for semantic segmentation. Specifically, our ViT model scores a mIoU of 75.30 on the PASCAL VOC dataset, significantly improving upon the baseline convolutional network's mIoU of 70.10. Additionally, our research highlights the benefits of using a hierarchical transformer model and masked image modeling as the self-supervised task. Notably, the segmentation quality of our self-supervised ViT model is comparable to that of models trained with extensive human annotations. Code and data are accessible at the provided URL.

A unified dark fluid model has been developed to simultaneously account for dark energy and dark matter. In this model, the equation of state for a dissipative fluid is defined as proportional to the sum of the fluid's density and pressure. Using the fluid's field equations within the framework of general relativity, a solution for the fluid's equation of state and density was derived, leading to a description of the fluid as a combination of a photon gas and a viscous fluid. By applying a new law for the dissipative coefficient, a fluid model was used to fit observational data from the supernova, cosmic microwave background radiation, and other sources, and the model was discovered to provide an excellent fit to the observed universe. Furthermore, the stability of the model was assessed by analyzing its acceleration and deceleration, and the model was discovered to be in good agreement with the observed expansion of the universe. Additionally, the model was discovered to be consistent with thermodynamic principles, and the model was discovered to be consistent with the observed acceleration of the universe's expansion, the cosmic microwave background radiation, and other observational data.

We present a straightforward proof that an infinite-dimensional differential equation exhibits unique solvability in both directions, thereby circumventing the typical issue of non-uniqueness associated with such problems. This allows us to demonstrate that the issue of non-uniqueness in certain ill-posed scenarios can be fully resolved. Moreover, the theory of infinite-dimensional differential equations can be utilized to tackle a long-standing problem in partial differential equations (PDEs), providing a solution in one direction that is unambiguous and analytically robust. Moreover, under specific conditions, our solution extends to provide uniqueness in both directions. These conditions relate to the stability of the underlying differential equation.

Recently, large text-conditioned generative models, such as GPT and DALL-E, have gained significant attention for their ability to process text and generate images. A critical issue with DALL-E is its inability to edit images based on textual guidance due to the lack of a pixel-level output cycle. To address this limitation, a novel approach is presented that incorporates a cycling pixel cycle ( CPC ) mechanism. CPC allows a generator to edit images based on the modifications specified in input text. Furthermore, semantic guidance (SEGA) is integrated into the model's training process to enhance its ability to generate images that match the modified prompts. During the CPC mechanism, noise and the modified image are mixed to produce the supporting signal for training the generator. SEGA is also utilized to compare the generated image with the original image's spectrum, further enhancing the model's editing capabilities. Both SEGA and the CPC mechanism can be applied to various generative models, and when combined with the GPT and U-Net architectures, they enable precise image editing based on text prompts.

Recent breakthroughs in deep learning have brought significant advancements to various applications of automatic data analysis, particularly in the accuracy of data predictions. However, when applying these techniques to sensitive areas such as medicine and law, simply relying on predictive performance may not provide a comprehensive understanding of prediction reliability. Therefore, developing methods to quantify uncertainty is essential. Here, we introduce a novel approach for refining uncertainty quantification in deep learning models by decoupling aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. This method involves training a Bayesian deep learning model on simulated data and then fine-tuning it on real-world data without retraining the entire model. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves uncertainty quantification accuracy, outperforming conventional methods even after extensive Bayesian model training.

Our research investigates the implications of the J/ψ particle decaying into invisible matter for light sterile neutrinos and sub-GeV dark matter particles, given current experimental constraints. We examine these scenarios within the framework of three-neutrino mixing and dark matter interactions. By considering the invisible decay J/ψ → ν_i ν̄_i as a gateway to new physics, we derive limits on neutral current couplings between neutrinos and matter, and solar neutrino oscillation parameters. This can be thought of an additional, hidden sector neutrino that's interacting via a standard model neutrino. Similarly, we examine the invisible decay in relation to dark matter-strange quark couplings that's relevant to dark matter detection via neutrinos and Z-boson mediated scattering. Our findings demonstrate that, under these conditions, the J/ψ decay provides more restrictive limits than existing bounds. Additionally, we represent these limits within global fits for neutrino oscillations and global limits for mediators of dark matter interactions.

High-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal tiny magnetic bright points, associated with extremely strong magnetic fields, present throughout the solar cycle, particularly prominent during the active phase.  Those located within granules can increase in brightness due to the rising of the granules.  However, when isolated from granules, their consistently elevated brightness remains unchanged by the solar cycle, leading us to speculate that they might be cooled down by an efficient process.  By analyzing the distributions of magnetic field strengths, areas, and sizes of solar images from the SOT/HiRES mission, we found that both the areas and strengths adhere to specific power-law distributions, whereas their strengths are significantly affected by the cooling process.  Furthermore, the distributions of their diameters and temperatures also follow power-laws, with the latter showing less contrast between active and quiet sun regions during the solar cycle, thereby supporting the hypothesis that magnetic bright points are efficiently cooled down.

Human vision can distinguish objects and actions using spatial or temporal data, but integrating these dimensions presents a complex challenge. This research introduces a novel approach, 3D convolutional neural networks, for a specific application, recognizing动作 in videos, where the networks can consider both spatial and motion characteristics. Extensive experiments comparing various architectures for a dataset of Italian actions demonstrate that 3D convolutional layers are effective, outperforming alternative methods. Additionally, optimization strategies using the Scaled Gradient-Coordinate (SGC) algorithm have been tested and shown to be a viable option. The dataset used for this study, called I3D, contains Italian videos of basic actions, along with corresponding labels.

Dark particles interacting through Abelian gauge forces and ordinary matter can be depicted by magnetic monopoles in their spacetime space. Specifically, the overproduction of these monopoles in the early universe poses challenges to the dark matter abundance, particularly those involving a hidden $U(1)_D$ gauge force, which allows couplings with both dark and ordinary matter. We investigate the constraints imposed by the halo ellipticity on these dark monopoles, space-like topological defects, whose shapes can be altered by the expansion of the universe. We space-like the ellipticity of the halo and space-like the ellipticity of the halo and space-like the ellipticity of the halo and space-like the

This research proposes a Swin-Transformer based method for forecasting weather patterns. The approach involves using a Swin-Transformer architecture with video inputs of historical weather data, which demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional weather prediction methods. To further improve efficiency in predicting future weather patterns, we developed a efficient layer for coarse-grained output forecasting. The method proves effective with experimental results using 40km resolution grid data. Additionally, we tackled the issue of handling varying grid data and created a solution for generating weather phasor time series from the grid. To address challenges in video upsampling, we incorporated a double-crop technique for testing. Overall, this research results in a high accuracy in forecasting future weather frames.

In models that expand on the electroweak sector, a basis can be found where the symmetry prevents coupling, leading to viable dark matter candidates. Specifically, we analyze the $S_3$-symmetric three-Higgs doublet models that allow soft breaking of this symmetry, finding that only a subset of this model's parameter space yields viable dark matter for both even and dark matter scenarios. In the scalar sector, vacuum stability is determined by a limited set of inequalities involving the Hessian of the potential and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-invariant quartic couplings. The relic dark matter abundance is computed numerically for various couplings and a $\mathbb{Z_2}$-symmetric parameter space, taking into account potential topological final state contributions.

A comprehensive study on the PPT square conjecture is presented with a notable achievement: the PPT square conjecture's validity has been rigorously demonstrated for the case involving finite-dimensional space.

Intracellular transportation is crucial for transporting vital substances, such as proteins and organelles, along the neuron's axon. Failure in this process can lead to the loss of synaptic connections and neurodegeneration. To address this issue, we suggest using a model that simulates molecular cargo movement in a neuron's axon using a Brownian ratchet mechanism, controlled by motor proteins moving in both directions on the axon's linear structure. We develop an algorithm for tuning model parameters to match experimental observations, such as the transport of mitochondria or other cargo, and observe how varying parameters affects the model's distribution. The model also enables researchers to develop hypotheses about protein trafficking and axonal transport based on the principles of reverse engineering.

Billion-dollar losses inflicted by banking fraud across the globe make graph-based fraud detection in transactions increasingly significant. In analyzing transaction patterns, researchers utilize graphs to identify novel and complex schemes. This research aims to identify real-world transaction network patterns, specifically network motifs within a heterogenous transaction dataset. We also present a method for generating genuine banking transaction graphs via randomization. The outcome of our preliminary analysis indicates that extracting network motifs can reveal meaningful and understandable patterns within the data.

We examine computer simulations of a white dwarf being stripped away by a black hole to find the characteristics of an electromagnetic signal produced by this process. As the white dwarf loses mass in this interaction and a black hole is surrounded by an accretion disc and clouds of debris, some material is flung out at high speeds, creating a distinct pattern of an electromagnetic signal and a gravitational wave signal. The material and radiation produced in this process include X-rays and gravitational waves that vary in intensity and duration over time. The shape and strength of the electromagnetic signal and the gravitational wave signal are related to the mass and size of the white dwarf star, suggesting that a certain type of white dwarf, the helium-rich one, would produce a particularly distinct pattern of an electromagnetic signal and a gravitational wave signal. This distinct pattern could be seen in the search for such signals in the event of a merging white dwarf stars found in other research, providing a novel and important finding.

Three-body $\tau$-decays, which involve light neutrinos and are a subprocess of $\tau$-decay, have been an underexplored area in electro-weak physics. These decays are sensitive to the presence of New Physics. Form factors, which are directly connected to hadron structure, are a crucial component in describing these forms. To gain insight into the hadronic structure, we applied the horizontal cut-off model to calculate the three-body hadronic form factors for the first time using a novel approach that combines the non-relativistic quark model and the horizontal cut-off model. Furthermore, we have computed the corresponding rates, angular distributions, and bremsstrahlung rates via Monte Carlo simulations.

Edward Tversky's Tversky ratio models, proposed in 1977, are among the most influential metrics for measuring list or set similarity, yet their interpolation as a metric has been a point of debate since then. A decision analysis by Meulman and Batyaev (2013) suggested an incomplete answer to this issue, prompting us to delve deeper and determine when the symmetric Tverscy ratio models meet the criteria to be considered a metric. Our investigation reveals that specific constraints must be placed on the parameters alpha and beta for these models to be effective in representing similarity. As a result, charts are provided to visually represent the regions where these metrics are applicable, along with suggestions as to which models are best suited for different uses.

Modern motion deblurring methods based on deep learning predominantly assume the presence of synthetic blur data for training. This assumption results in a lack of effectiveness when applied to real-world images, as evidenced by the decline in performance on the DSR dataset. To tackle this problem, we introduce a novel, real blur data-driven semi-supervised motion deblurring approach, which leverages a small set of labeled and a larger set of unlabeled images. Our method employs self-supervised semi-supervised data augmentation techniques, including random mosaic, to enhance the model's performance, and also utilizes a kernel-based self-enemy data augmentation method to produce a diverse training set. By integrating these techniques, we achieve superior motion deblurring performance, outperforming existing methods while accounting for the costs of training and inference.

Hebbian learning enables autonomous skill acquisition through a simple principle: "neurons that fire together, wire together." This mechanism allows for continuous learning without the need for outside assistance. Our research focuses on implementing a form of local plasticity in a swarm of micro-air-vehicles that function as a single, unified unit. Each vehicle is part of a collective that maintains a stable shape and structure as it moves. By utilizing a hybrid control system that combines hebbian learning with leader-followers-based coordination, the vehicles learn complex maneuvers to track a moving target. Our approach demonstrates that a small number of autonomous vehicles can learn complex cooperative tasks through hebbian learning, which is both biologically inspired and computationally efficient.

The ultrapower of any ordered set is created as a refined version of the set itself by taking into account infinite sequences of elements from it. This process involves dividing the sequences into classes according to a set of rules defined by an ultrafilter, leading to a set that always satisfies a fundamental property of ordered sets. It turns out that a set's openness determines its ability to fulfill the open completeness property in the refined version, whereas its original cardinality dictates whether the refined version is complete.

Scientific breakthroughs in data-driven science rely on accurately representing the underlying phenomena through computational models, which are then evaluated against extensive experimental data. As machine learning techniques accelerate, they are becoming increasingly utilized to develop these models, raising the challenge of objectively assessing their performance against a vast array of possible alternatives. To address this, data-centric indices, which measure the discrepancy between predicted and observed data, are employed. To further refine this process, we propose representing the characteristics of scientific datasets in a standardized, high-dimensional space. We achieve this by introducing a generic embedding approach rooted in information theory and dimensionality reduction, which has been successfully tested across diverse scientific domains. By analyzing the impact of various factors on the resulting dataset representations, we provide a framework for understanding scientific data, which can be applied to evaluate the accuracy of computational models and facilitate their objective comparison.

Hadwiger's Coloring Conjecture asserts that every graph with t color classes must contain a complete graph with t vertices. This is equivalent to stating that a graph with no complete graph with t+1 vertices within it can be colored using only t color classes. While it is known that the chromatic number is O(log n), where n represents the size of the graph, progress in this area has been limited. Our work presents a breakthrough by introducing a family of graphs where each graph can be colored using just three color classes and simultaneously contains a complete graph with four vertices. This graph exhibits a structure in which four complete subgraphs, each with an arbitrary number of vertices, are connected in such a way that no two of these subgraphs are connected.

This research introduces an advanced algorithm for graph signal recovery, leveraging the graph Fourier transform in the sparse domain. By transforming an optimization problem with a kernelized approach, we estimate the kernel width adaptively, eliminating the need for prior knowledge. The algorithm's performance relies heavily on the adaptive selection of kernel widths, and thus, we propose two methods for their coherent calculation. Moreover, theoretical analysis guides the development of these algorithms, facilitating their application in scenarios where the eigenspectrum of the graph Laplacian is unknown. Experimental results confirm that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing approaches while greatly reducing computational complexity.

The potential benefit of entangled atomic energy-time correlations for enhanced atom interferometry is explored, particularly in scenarios influenced by technical noise. This investigation focuses on common types of technical noise and evaluates their impact on entangled vs. non-entangled atoms. The considered cases include detection efficiency, index of refraction fluctuations, and phase modulation, all of which can be understood through a fundamental model. The results reveal that while certain forms of technical noise can efficiently utilize the correlations in entangled atomic pairs, other noise types do not yield similar results. The analysis also indicates that a detection scheme capable of overcoming efficiency limitations is necessary to enhance interferometry through entanglement. The study serves as a foundational understanding of the practical application of entangled atomic correlations for enhanced atom interferometry.

We investigate a variational problem related to the anisotropic $p$-Laplace operator, specifically seeking a set with optimal volume to minimize this eigenvalue. Our main contribution is a existence proof for optimal sets, which can be applied to a specific case of a free discontinuity problem modeling anhealable material transformation. This application involves a non-divergence type free boundary problem where we prove the existence of optimal sets for a specific variational problem involving a free boundary with minimal surface area, regardless of the boundary condition's shape.

Deep Neural Networks used in machine learning have developed a variant, 
Graph Neural Networks, which enable processing of data represented in graph form. 
A graph can be used to represent relationships between objects in real-world 
scenarios such as computer vision, medical diagnosis, and social network 
analysis. Learning from graphs typically involves GCNNs, where GCNNs use 
node-based operations to combine input from neighboring nodes through 
specialized layers, including convolution and aggregation. Among these, 
the convolution layer plays a crucial role in feature extraction. This study 
investigates existing graph convolution layers and their implementations, 
focusing on defining what constitutes a valid graph convolution. We also 
compare the performance of different graph convolution layers, analyzing 
their trade-offs between theoretical guarantees, computational efficiency, 
and practical performance. Our research aims to provide a framework for 
designing novel graph convolution layers.

A significant challenge in developing neural dependency parsers is acquiring a substantial amount of annotated data due to the labor-intensive and expertise-intensive nature of the process. Consequently, researchers have been interested in methods that minimize the requirements for large-scale data labeling. Self-supervised pretraining has demonstrated remarkable progress in various natural language tasks, and this paper explores its potential in neural dependency parsing through unsupervised and supervised evaluation. To address data labeling issues, we developed a novel pretraining task that utilizes linear projections without contextual information to predict dependency heads and directions. Moreover, our comparative study of pretraining methods reveals that our parser achieves superior performance with minimal training data, and often surpasses the best performance with ample training data.
